title: Captain Hildethrax
dek: A Rahu captain who sets boundaries, arranges supplies and leads a peace delegation through the night. His courteous welcome carries firm expectations about rank, obedience and what cooperation should return to his people.

facts.Title: Captain
facts.Recovered scenes: 31 May 2024–23 June 2025 · selected quest and associated-room records

sources: Quest-RP thread archive and association map — supplied 11 October 2026; accessible-room evidence; posting dates America/New_York
body:
Captain Hildethrax is a senior Rahu officer whose responsibilities bring together investigation, security, logistics, institutional access, and implementation. He serves within Witch Queen Ephraith’s state on Prima, and introduces himself with precise attention to title, honor, and standing.

I am the honorable Captain Hildethrax, second rank.Captain Hildethrax

The meaning of second rank remains unresolved. His authority is established through what he does; the title alone does not make him second-in-command of the entire Rahu.

31 May 2024: the Edran investigation

When the Rahu acolyte Edran is murdered, Hildethrax knows the condition of the scene and the evidence behind the suspicion of Nienna. He confirms that the body has not been touched and reports that she was found in trees across the river to the west, with wet clothing.

The accusation is later disproved. Ephraith accepts the evidence clearing Nienna and provides restitution. Hildethrax’s involvement establishes an investigative role, while the recovered account gives no basis for treating him as a knowing participant in a frame-up.

18 June 2024: the cost of assistance

Asked whether Rahu assistance comes without strings, Hildethrax says that the bank can bear a short-term burden because it expects value over time. Loans are not free. Competition for scarce magical objects is, in his words, “Honest competition.” He names material interests plainly rather than pretending resources are unlimited.

7 August 2024: rank and guarded knowledge

Olokun asks to consult Rahu contamination records. Hildethrax refuses access because the visitors lack the required rank. The archives are guarded, and their contents have both cultural and strategic value.

Knowledge is sacred....and valuable.Captain Hildethrax

His refusal has limits. He is willing to send Rahu personnel to investigate credible contamination reports, even while withholding protected records and methods. A threat to Rahu interests can change the case for committing resources.

He also explains a broad path toward membership: living among the Rahu, swearing allegiance on sacred ground, and undergoing initiation. That outline does not make him the final ritual authority or disclose the private rites themselves.

Talon’s wound and the limits of hospitality

Hildethrax offers Strange Talon as an investigator, calling him “our best” and “a true bastion of our forces.” The offer is useful and pointed: the officer the outsiders need is also the man the Rahu believe they have wronged.

When the grievance is challenged, Hildethrax points to the wound and weapon evidence. The archive sometimes calls this official Swift Talon or Sir Talon; the wider recovered Rahu material identifies the intelligence figure as Strange Talon. Those scene variants do not establish a separate senior official.

Olokun invokes the offending adventurer’s wider heroic history. Hildethrax focuses on the injury under Rahu jurisdiction. His patience ends when guests continue questioning his people inside their home; he tells them to leave and perhaps not return. The dispute exposes how differently adventurers and state officials weigh reputation, evidence, and sovereignty.

22 December 2024: at the door

At a formal gathering Hildethrax personally checks invitations. His repeated “Invitation, please” shows a captain enforcing an ordinary rule of access as directly as he guards more consequential institutions.

20 January 2025: agreements need implementation

At the inter-faction council he greets Yllandaer cordially. His severity depends on the circumstances; he can smile and welcome an outsider’s interest.

When Ambassador Sophina agrees in principle to sell food to Fenwick d’Jorasco, she directs him to work out the arrangements with Hildethrax. Transport is expensive, and drawing down Rahu reserves carries risk. Negotiation must become a practical plan for moving supplies.

The operational officer

Ephraith exercises sovereignty, Sophina represents Rahu interests diplomatically, Talon gathers intelligence, and Yami no Majo handles specialist knowledge and teaching. Hildethrax’s recovered work turns decisions into procedures, guarded doors, investigations, and logistics. These observed functions leave the complete chain of command open.

He is proud, practical, hierarchical, protective, and capable of cooperation within firm boundaries. His species, age, appointment, exact authority over Talon, individual battlefield actions in the 2025 war, and later fate remain unknown.

Sewer aid and a coastal outpost

After the Kinnich Ahau festival, Hildethrax clarifies that Rahu materials are intended for Eovar’s sewer repairs; what the Rahu want in exchange is land for a coastal outpost. Fenwick thanks him for food and sewer designs, and promises timely payment. This is a negotiation and an obligation, not evidence that the outpost was built. Hildethrax describes the Rahu as guarding their own territory rather than joining a general war against Death; that remains his stated policy.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

Courtesy, rank and the people expected to obey

Hildethrax’s first embassy reception is courteous, but its bows are not equal. He answers the visitors with shallower bows and takes pride in the idea that a Rahu officer should know history and morality as well as warfare. Sildithas’s questions draw a brisk defense of excellence across every discipline.

When the conversation turns to manual workers, Hildethrax says those who do not seek higher standards must listen to those who do. Olokun asks whether he means slavery. The captain insists the arrangement is a choice and describes security and material provision in return. He also describes banishment, loss of housing and work, and erasure of a person’s name for refusing the expected obligations. His account sets the costs beside his claim of fairness; it is not independent proof that every worker has the freedom he describes.

His economic explanation is equally direct. The embassy studies the unfamiliar magic brought by adventurers while the bank expects to gain wealth and influence. He welcomes the prospect of mutual benefit and says plainly that lending is meant to pay. The reception records a state offering help on terms it expects to profit from.

The contact after the ambassador leaves

After the council, Sophina directs Lionel to Hildethrax because the captain is taking over local operations. Lionel can continue helping while retaining his refusal to shed blood under Rahu law. The handoff identifies the officer through whom further practical contact should run; it does not turn the captain into the final judge of every dispute.

That arrangement fits the other recovered exchanges: Sophina agrees to food sales, Hildethrax handles transport, and later he explains what the Rahu want for sewer assistance. The division is useful precisely because an agreement still needs someone to implement it. The proposed coastal outpost remains a negotiation, with no recovered confirmation that it was built.

Walking the former enemies toward the Queen

When the peace company approaches Rahu territory, Hildethrax is there to escort it. He acknowledges their strength and promises no harm unless provoked, while still addressing Olokun as a traitor. Courtesy at the threshold has not erased his political judgment.

He leads them through the night along mountain roads. At dawn a pond and ceremonial gate mark the next stage of the approach. Asked why the war began, he yields the explanation to Hoshi Daemon and bows low to the holy man. His work here is guiding and guarding the delegation; the Queen’s terms remain hers to negotiate.

Anky asks to pray for the dead on both sides, and Hildethrax permits it. He then leads the company toward the Queen’s retreat. A captain who has previously expelled unwelcome guests now brings adversaries into a diplomatic meeting without pretending they have become friends.

chapters.title: A courteous welcome with unequal terms
The officer and the limits of his record

profile.personality: Proud, exact about hierarchy and capable of both patient explanation and abrupt dismissal. He defends the Rahu’s account of merit and acknowledges their commercial interests. He can call a former enemy a traitor and still honor the escort’s promise of safety.
profile.achievements: Reports evidence in the Edran investigation, receives embassy visitors, guards access to archives, offers investigative cooperation, checks invitations and coordinates food and infrastructure negotiations. Later conducts the peace company along the overnight approach to the Queen. His stated second rank does not establish that he is second-in-command of the whole Rahu.
profile.relationships: Ephraith exercises sovereignty; Sophina delegates practical follow-up; Talon supplies intelligence and a grievance Hildethrax takes seriously. Nienna’s exoneration remains the outcome of the earlier case. Olokun repeatedly presses his boundaries, while Anky’s prayer for both sides receives his permission during the peace approach.
